quests.title: Find Orion's Belt
quests.intro: Orion the Hunter is one of the easiest star pictures to spot. His belt is three stars in a neat little row!

steps.clue: Look for three stars in a row in the hunter's belt! Click the one in the MIDDLE.
steps.hint: The belt is between bright red Betelgeuse and bright blue Rigel.
steps.fact: Alnilam is a blue supergiant about 2,000 light-years away. It shines hundreds of thousands of times brighter than our Sun!

steps.clue: Great! Now find the belt star on the LEFT end (the one closer to Betelgeuse's side, going down).
steps.hint: It sits right next to Alnilam, on the side toward the bottom-left.
steps.fact: Alnitak is actually a family of stars orbiting each other. Near it is the famous Horsehead Nebula, a dark cloud shaped like a horse's head!

steps.clue: Last one! Click the belt star on the OTHER end of the row.
steps.hint: It's the belt star closest to the right, a little higher than the other two.
steps.fact: Mintaka sits almost exactly on the sky's equator, so people everywhere on Earth can see it, from the North Pole to the South Pole!

quests.title: Meet the Brightest Stars
quests.intro: Some stars look super bright because they are huge, and some because they are close. Let's meet the champions!

steps.clue: Find the BRIGHTEST star in the whole night sky. It's called the Dog Star!
steps.hint: Follow Orion's belt down and to the left, and you'll bump right into it.
steps.fact: Sirius is only 8.6 light-years away, which is super close for a star. That's one reason it looks so bright!

steps.clue: Now find the second-brightest star. It's far in the southern sky.
steps.hint: It's below Sirius, much further south, almost all by itself.
steps.fact: Canopus is a giant star about 300 light-years away. Spacecraft have used it like a compass to steer through space!

steps.clue: Find a bright ORANGE star. Its name means 'Guardian of the Bear'.
steps.hint: Follow the curve of the Big Dipper's handle and 'arc to Arcturus'!
steps.fact: Arcturus is an orange giant, about 25 times wider than our Sun. Its light helped open the 1933 World's Fair in Chicago!

steps.clue: Last one! Find a bright blue-white star in the little harp constellation, Lyra.
steps.hint: It's a very bright star with a small parallelogram of stars next to it.
steps.fact: Vega spins so fast that it's squashed, like a ball that's being stretched at its middle! In about 12,000 years it will be our North Star.

quests.title: Our Closest Neighbors
quests.intro: Which stars live closest to our Sun? Let's visit our neighbors in space!

steps.clue: Find the closest bright star to us! It's a bright star low in the southern sky, in the Centaur.
steps.hint: It's one of two bright 'pointer' stars near the Southern Cross. Pick the brighter one!
steps.fact: Rigil Kentaurus (Alpha Centauri) is only 4.3 light-years away. Light from it takes about 4 years to reach your eyes!

steps.clue: Now find the brightest star in the sky. It's also one of our closest neighbors!
steps.hint: Look for the super bright star near Orion, down and to the left of the belt.
steps.fact: Sirius has a tiny partner star called Sirius B, a 'white dwarf' that is about the size of Earth but as heavy as the Sun!

steps.clue: Find the 'Little Dog' star. It's another close neighbor, near Sirius.
steps.hint: It's a bright star above and to the left of Orion, making a triangle with Betelgeuse and Sirius.
steps.fact: Procyon is about 11 light-years away. Its name means 'before the dog' because it rises just before Sirius, the Dog Star!

quests.title: Big Dipper Hunt
quests.intro: The Big Dipper looks like a giant spoon (or a pot with a handle). It's part of the Great Bear!

steps.clue: Find the star at the top corner of the Dipper's cup, the one furthest from the handle.
steps.hint: The cup has four stars. Dubhe is the top one on the side away from the handle.
steps.fact: Dubhe and Merak are called the 'Pointer Stars'. Draw a line through them and it points to Polaris, the North Star!

steps.clue: Now find the star right below Dubhe, at the bottom of the cup.
steps.hint: It's the other 'pointer' star, just under Dubhe.
steps.fact: Merak is about 80 light-years away and is twice as big as our Sun.

steps.clue: Find the middle star of the Dipper's handle.
steps.hint: The handle has three stars in a curve. Pick the one in the middle.
steps.fact: Mizar has a tiny buddy star called Alcor. Long ago, people tested their eyesight by trying to see both!

steps.clue: Last one! Find the star at the very end of the handle.
steps.hint: Follow the handle all the way out to its tip.
steps.fact: Alkaid is a hot blue star about 100 light-years away. Its name means 'the leader' in Arabic.

quests.title: Red Giants vs Blue Giants
quests.intro: Stars come in colors! Red stars are cooler, and blue stars are super hot. Can you find them?

steps.clue: Find the big RED star on Orion's shoulder.
steps.hint: It's the bright orange-red star above the belt, on the left side.
steps.fact: Betelgeuse is so huge that if it were where our Sun is, it would swallow Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars!

steps.clue: Now find a bright BLUE star at Orion's knee, on the opposite corner from Betelgeuse.
steps.hint: It's below the belt on the right side.
steps.fact: Rigel is a blue supergiant, about 120,000 times brighter than the Sun. Blue stars are much hotter than red ones!

steps.clue: Find the red heart of the Scorpion. Its name means 'rival of Mars'!
steps.hint: Look for a reddish star in the middle of a long, curvy line of stars shaped like a scorpion.
steps.fact: Antares is about 700 times wider than our Sun. It looks reddish, just like the planet Mars.

steps.clue: Last one! Find a bright BLUE-white star in Virgo.
steps.hint: Follow the Big Dipper's handle: 'arc to Arcturus, then speed on to Spica'.
steps.fact: Spica is actually two hot blue stars spinning around each other so fast that they're squished into egg shapes!
